title: Ferrari F40 vs Porsche 959: The Difference Nobody Explains
description:
Two supercars from the same year, both born from the end of Group B racing. One has rear-wheel drive, a twin-turbo V eight and no radio. The other has all-wheel drive, an adjustable ride height and a flat six that Porsche built at a loss. One was made in over thirteen hundred copies. The other in fewer than three hundred. This is the real difference between the Ferrari F forty and the Porsche nine fifty-nine. Here is the twist. The Porsche was faster at Nardò, by eighteen kilometres per hour or more. It was also, on the sources we read, cheaper than it cost to build, by more than half. And the Ferrari, the simpler car, is the one that was built in larger numbers, and the one that people queued to buy. Let us go through the numbers, and where the sources disagree.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
